question: In badminton, how high above the ground is the net positioned at the centre?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**5 feet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **badminton**, the **height of the net** is a critical factor as it ensures fair play and adherence to the rules of the game.
 
• The net is positioned at a height of **5 feet** in the center from the ground.
 
• The height is slightly higher at the edges, which is set at **5 feet 1 inch**, as per the official guidelines provided by the **Badminton World Federation (BWF).**
 
• The net is made from **dark-colored material** with a white tape running along the top edge, ensuring visibility during matches.
 
• The net height is adjusted and measured carefully before matches in professional tournaments to maintain **consistency and fairness.**
 
• The height of 5 feet allows players to execute various shots such as **smashes, clears, drops, and net shots** effectively while maintaining the strategic depth of the game.
 
• Adhering to this height ensures standardized gameplay across courts worldwide, supporting the idea of uniform rules for both recreational and competitive badminton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here is a list of the names of badminton cups:

 
 
• Thomas Cup: International men's team badminton championship
 
• Uber Cup: International women's team badminton championship
 
• Sudirman Cup: International mixed team badminton championship
 
• BWF World Championships: Individual badminton championship featuring singles, doubles, and mixed doubles
 
• BWF World Junior Championships: Individual badminton championship for players under the age of 19
 
• BWF World Senior Championships: Individual badminton championship for players over the age of 35
 
• BWF World Tour Super 1000, Super 750, Super 500, and Super 300 tournaments: Series of badminton tournaments held throughout the year.
